in_hebrew.name: לורדס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A name derived from the Hebrew words לור (lur) which means 'mount' and דס (des) which means 'gods'. It is often translated as 'Mount of the Gods'.

in_greek.name: Λουρδές
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Lurdes has no direct meaning in Greek, but it is the transliteration of the Spanish name Lourdes, which in turn comes from the Latin name Lourdia.

in_latin.name: Lourdia
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Lourdes in Latin is believed to derive from the word 'lourdus', which means 'heavy, weighty, or burdensome'. This name may have been given due to the town's reputation as a place of pilgrimage and healing, as pilgrims would carry heavy burdens in their journey to Lourdes.

in_english.name: Lurdes
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lurdes in English is the same as its Spanish and Latin forms, as it comes directly from these languages.

data.cultural_impact: Lourdes is a renowned pilgrimage site for Christians around the world, especially Catholics. It is located in southern France and has been a place of devotion since the 19th century when the Virgin Mary is said to have appeared to Bernadette Soubirous, a young girl. This Marian apparition has inspired countless stories of faith, miracles, and healings. Lourdes is a symbol of both religious and cultural heritage, with numerous pilgrims making their way to the site each year to experience its spiritual power.
data.spiritual_significance: Lourdes holds great significance for Christians, not just as a historical site but also as a place of faith, hope, and healing. The apparition of Mary to Bernadette Soubirous is believed by many to be a divine intervention, reminding us of God's unending love and mercy. The water from the spring in Lourdes is believed to hold healing powers, drawing millions to its banks each year. Lourdes represents a deep connection between the divine and human beings, emphasizing the spiritual journey we all undertake in our lives.
